cover_title: RGB Roof Top Lighting – Granada Business Park

blocks.text: This Scope of Work (SOW) defines the requirements for the assessment, lighting design, supply, installation, programming, testing, and commissioning of an architectural RGB roof-top lighting system for the HR buildings (A1 to A6) and LR buildings (B1 to B4) at Granada Business Park, Riyadh.

The Contractor shall assess the current architectural design of each building and propose RGB lighting that suits and enhances that architecture, replacing the existing roof-top lighting. The work shall be delivered as a complete turnkey solution, including a central DMX control system and a 5-year comprehensive warranty.

The objective of this work is to give the buildings a coherent, high-quality night-time identity through architectural RGB lighting designed around the form, features and materials of each building. The Contractor shall assess the buildings, develop a lighting concept for Client approval, and then design, supply, install, program and commission the approved system.
Key objectives include:

items: Assess the current architectural design of each building (roof profile, parapets, crowns, screens, cladding and finishes) and identify the features to be lit.
Propose a lighting concept that highlights the architecture and creates a unified identity across the HR and LR buildings.
Determine the suitable fixture types, locations, quantities, beam angles and colour effects for each building through the approved design.
Supply RGB fixtures of a Saudi local brand as first preference, or an approved alternative brand where no suitable local brand is available.
Provide a central DMX512 control system allowing each building to be controlled as an individual zone, as well as master control of all buildings.
Replace the existing roof-top lighting, including all power and DMX cabling, containment and associated electrical works.
Program static, dynamic and occasion scenes (Saudi National Day, Founding Day, Ramadan and Eid) with automatic astronomical scheduling.
Provide a 5-year comprehensive warranty covering fixtures, drivers, DMX components, controller and software.

blocks.text: This SOW does not fix the number or type of lighting fixtures. The Contractor shall determine the fixture types, locations and quantities for each building based on the site survey, the architectural assessment and the lighting design approved by the Client.

The BOQ in Appendix A is a pricing template, organized per building for the HR and LR buildings. The Contractor shall enter the proposed fixture types, quantities and unit prices for each building. The final number of units for each building shall be as per the site survey and the approved lighting design. The Contractor's unit rates shall remain fixed and shall apply to the final approved quantities.

columns: Areas to be Assessed and Lit
rows: Roof top, including roof-level architectural features (parapets, crowns, screens, cladding edges)
Roof top, including roof-level architectural features and any upper-level features identified in the assessment

blocks.text: Site Survey and Existing Condition Assessment
Carry out a comprehensive site survey of all 10 buildings and verify the existing roof-top lighting, electrical infrastructure and installation conditions.

items: Record the existing roof-top installation, its condition and the items to be removed.
Verify existing power points, lighting distribution boards, spare capacity, earthing and control (timers/contactors).
Assess roof access, parapet and structure conditions for mounting fixtures, and any work-at-height constraints.
Identify cable routes for power and DMX cabling on roofs and between buildings.
Confirm the location of the central DMX controller and the network/backbone route between the HR and LR buildings.

blocks.text: Architectural Assessment of the Buildings

items: Obtain and review the available architectural drawings and elevations of the buildings from Osool.
Study the architecture of each building: roof profile, massing, parapets, crowns, screens, vertical and horizontal lines, cladding materials, finishes and colours.
Identify the key architectural features to be highlighted and the surfaces to be avoided (glazing, reflective cladding).
Identify the main viewing points and distances (approach roads, entrances, plazas and neighboring areas).
Assess the relationship between the HR and LR buildings to achieve a unified identity across the business park.
Assess glare and light-spill impact on occupants, neighboring buildings and roads.
Submit an Architectural Assessment Report with photographs, marked-up elevations and the proposed lighting approach for each building.

blocks.text: Lighting Concept and Design

items: Develop a lighting concept for each building that suits and enhances its architecture, with a consistent identity across the HR and LR buildings.
Select suitable fixture types for each feature (e.g. floodlights, wall washers, linear grazers, pixel/dot fixtures) with appropriate beam angles and output.
Provide night-time visualizations (photo-realistic renders) of each building type, showing white and colour scenes.
Provide lighting calculations (DIALux or equal) showing light levels, uniformity and glare control.
Provide an estimate of the total connected load and annual energy consumption.
Present the concept to Osool, incorporate comments and obtain written approval before detailed design.
Prepare the detailed design: fixture layout per building, quantity schedule by type, mounting details, power single-line diagram, DMX riser diagram and addressing plan.

blocks.text: Mock-up and Sample Approval

items: Install a mock-up of the proposed fixtures on one HR building and one LR building, as agreed with Osool.
Demonstrate colour quality, output, beam angles and scenes during a night-time inspection with the Client.
Adjust the design as required and obtain written approval before ordering the full quantity.

blocks.text: Supply of RGB Lighting Fixtures (Saudi Brand Preferred)

items: Supply RGB/RGBW LED fixtures of a Saudi local brand, manufactured or assembled in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as first preference.
For a Saudi brand, submit the manufacturer commercial registration, factory address and local-content / Saudi Made certificate.

Where no suitable Saudi brand is available, the Contractor may offer an alternative brand, stating the reason, the country of origin and the local agent/distributor in KSA. Alternative brands are subject to Client approval.
Any offered brand shall have SASO/SALEEM conformity certificates, local after-sales support and spare-parts availability in KSA for the full 5-year warranty period.
Supply all mounting brackets, glare shields/visors where required, and stainless-steel fixings.
All fixtures shall meet the minimum technical requirements below.

rows: As per the approved lighting design (floodlights, wall washers, linear grazers, pixel/dot fixtures, etc.)
RGBW (RGB + white) preferred; RGB acceptable where approved in the design
Native DMX512-A, RDM preferred; 16-bit flicker-free dimming
IP66 minimum (IP67 for exposed roof edges); IK08
Die-cast aluminium, marine-grade powder coat, tempered glass; beam angles per design
220–240 V AC, 60 Hz; PF ≥ 0.9; THD < 20 %; built-in surge protection ≥ 6 kV
Binned LEDs; uniform colour between fixtures of the same type
SASO / SALEEM, CE or equal, LM-79 / LM-80 test reports

blocks.text: DMX Control System

items: Supply, install and configure a central DMX512 / Art-Net (or sACN) controller with scene memory and astronomical scheduling.
Provide DMX splitters/boosters, decoders, network nodes, terminators and surge protection for every DMX line.
Configure each building as an individual zone, with sub-zones per architectural feature, and master control of all buildings.
Provide a UPS-backed controller enclosure, network switch and a control tablet/PC with licensed programming software.
The system shall restore the last scene automatically after a power failure.
Size the system for the final approved number of fixtures plus 25 % spare channels.
Provide non-expiring software licenses, programmer-level access passwords and configuration backups at handover.

blocks.text: Power and DMX Cabling and Containment

items: Supply and install outdoor/UV-rated copper power cables sized for a maximum 3 % voltage drop.
Supply and install shielded twisted-pair 120 Ω DMX cable within DMX segment limits, with fiber or outdoor CAT6 backbone between buildings where required.
Install all outdoor cables in GI conduit, UV-resistant flexible conduit or cable tray; no exposed cable on roofs.
Connect the existing lighting distribution boards with new MCBs/RCBOs and contactors as required and verify DB load and earthing.
Seal and waterproof all roof and wall penetrations to the Client standard.

blocks.text: Removal of Existing Roof-Top Lighting

items: Safely isolate, disconnect and remove the existing roof-top lighting fixtures, ballasts, ignitors and redundant cabling identified in the site survey.
Hand over removed items to the Osool store or dispose of them as instructed by the Client.
Make good any damage caused to roofs, parapets and finishes during removal.

blocks.text: Installation and Workmanship Requirements

items: All installation work shall be carried out by competent and suitably experienced personnel.
Install fixtures as per the approved design, aimed and locked, with fixtures and cables concealed from main viewpoints where possible.
Protect existing operational systems, roof waterproofing and building services during work.
Label all fixtures (with DMX address), cables, junction boxes and panels, matching the as-built drawings.
Any required dismantling, reinstatement, minor associated work and making good necessary to complete the installation shall be included.
No circuit shall be energized until the required inspections and testing have been completed.

blocks.text: Programming and Scene Configuration

items: Address all fixtures and configure the DMX universes as per the approved addressing plan.
Program a minimum of 20 scenes designed around the architecture, including static white, single colours, colour fades and chases.
Program occasion scenes for Saudi National Day, Founding Day, Ramadan and Eid.
Configure the weekly/annual schedule and astronomical on/off times.
Configure password-protected user levels for operation from the tablet/PC.

blocks.text: Testing, Commissioning and Handover
Pre-commissioning

items: Visual inspection of all newly installed fixtures, brackets, cabling and containment.
Insulation resistance and earth continuity tests on all power circuits.
Verification of terminations, labeling, waterproofing of penetrations and physical condition.
Verification of DMX signal integrity, termination and addressing before functional testing.

blocks.text: Functional Testing

items: Test every fixture on all colour channels (R, G, B, W) and dimming range.
Test each building zone individually and the master control of all buildings.
Test all programmed scenes, schedules and astronomical timing.
Test automatic scene recovery after power interruption.
Carry out a night-time inspection with the Client to confirm the result matches the approved design and visualizations, and complete final aiming adjustments.
The lighting system shall be completed and handed over in a healthy state, without any faulty fixture, channel or control function.

rows: 100 % of installed fixtures operating on all channels, uniform colour across each feature
Night-time result matches the approved concept and visualizations
No flicker or signal loss; all fixtures respond at their assigned address
All 10 building zones and ≥ 20 scenes operate from the controller and tablet
Automatic on/off and occasion scenes run as programmed
Test results within limits of SBC 401; no nuisance tripping
Last scene restored automatically after power interruption

blocks.text: Handover Requirements

items: Final testing and commissioning reports.
DMX addressing plan, controller programming and configuration backup files.
Software license documentation and access passwords.
As-built drawings: fixture layouts, power SLDs and DMX riser diagrams.
Equipment data sheets and manufacturer documentation for all supplied items.
Record of removed fixtures handed over to the Osool store.
Training for the Osool operations and maintenance team (minimum 2 sessions).
Outstanding snag list, if any, with agreed closure status.
Formal initial handover following successful completion and acceptance of the works.

blocks.text: Maintenance, Warranty and Defects Rectification

The Contractor shall provide a 5-year comprehensive warranty from the date of final handover, covering the RGB fixtures, LED drivers, DMX decoders/splitters, controller, software and installation workmanship. Faulty items shall be replaced free of charge, including labor and access equipment.
The Contractor shall respond within 48 hours of notification and complete the repair or replacement within 7 days. Replacement fixtures shall match the colour and output of the installed batch.

sections.heading: Applicable Standards, Codes and Authority Requirements

blocks.text: The Contractor shall execute the works in accordance with the applicable electrical and lighting requirements, approved project requirements, manufacturer recommendations, and requirements of the relevant authority having jurisdiction.

Where an applicable standard, authority requirement or existing approved system requirement is more stringent than the Contractor's proposed solution, the more stringent requirement shall be followed subject to Client approval.
Following is a non-exhaustive description of relevant Codes/ Standards that may be referenced.

rows: Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization product conformity
Degrees of protection provided by enclosures (IP code)
Asynchronous serial digital data transmission standard for controlling lighting equipment
Remote Device Management over DMX512 networks
Photometric and LED lumen maintenance testing
Guide on the limitation of the effects of obtrusive light from outdoor lighting installations
Local Content and Government Procurement Authority – local content requirements

blocks.text: No specific exclusions are identified. Civil or structural modifications to the buildings, and upgrades of main LV panels or transformers, are excluded unless identified during the site survey. Any work outside the items listed in this SOW/ BOQ, or any additional work arising from the site survey, shall be clearly identified by the Contractor and shall require Client approval before execution.

items: Site survey and verification of existing lighting and electrical conditions.
Architectural assessment of all HR and LR buildings.
Lighting concept, night-time visualizations, lighting calculations, detailed design and technical submittals.
Mock-up installation and sample approval.
Supply of RGB LED fixtures as per the approved design (Saudi local brand preferred, or approved alternative), with brackets and accessories.
Supply and installation of the central DMX control system, network components and software licenses.
All power and DMX cabling, containment and connections to existing distribution boards.
Removal of existing roof-top lighting, and handover/disposal as instructed.
Installation, addressing, programming and scene configuration.
Testing, commissioning, final functional verification and approval from the appropriate Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), where required.
Training, documentation, configuration backups and handover.
5-year comprehensive warranty.
The lighting design shall be prepared by a qualified lighting designer with proven experience in architectural lighting; CVs and a portfolio of similar projects shall be submitted with the offer.
All supplied equipment and materials shall be new and suitable for Saudi outdoor conditions (high ambient temperature, UV, sand and dust).
Saudi local brands shall be given preference; any alternative brand shall be approved by the Client and supported by valid SASO/SALEEM certificates and local after-sales support.
The Contractor shall ensure that all workmanship and installation are of a professional standard acceptable to the manufacturer.
All testing shall be performed using suitable calibrated test equipment.
Any failed test shall be investigated, rectified and repeated until the required result is achieved.
DMX programming and controller configuration shall be performed by engineers trained or certified by the manufacturer.

The Contractor shall comply with the Client's HSE requirements and all applicable site safety procedures, including, but not limited to, work at height, roof access and electrical isolation requirements.
The Contractor shall obtain the required permits and approvals before commencing work.
Appropriate isolation/LOTO procedures shall be applied where required for safe execution.
All roof-top work shall use certified fall protection, scaffolding, lifting equipment or rope access as applicable.
Work areas shall be maintained clean and safe throughout the execution and removed fixtures shall be disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner.
The Contractor shall protect occupants, tenants, existing systems and building operations during the works.

The contractor must ensure that a qualified representative (Project Engineer/ Project manager) is always present on-site during the execution of the project.
If the contractor fails to have a representative present, a penalty of **2,500 SAR per day** will be applied for each day of absence.
**Progress Reporting:** The contractor is required to submit progress reports on a **weekly and monthly basis** as follows:
**Weekly Reports:** Must include the status of work compared to the project timeline, key milestones achieved, resources utilized, and any risks identified.
**Monthly Reports:** Must include a comprehensive overview of progress, any changes to the project plan, and a forecast for the upcoming month.
Failure to submit progress reports on time will incur penalties as follows:
**Weekly Reports:** Penalty of **2,000 SAR** for each late or missed report.
**Monthly Reports:** Penalty of **5,000 SAR** for each late or missed report.

If the work does not meet the technical specifications as outlined in the scope of work or the quality of the work is deemed unsatisfactory by the client, the contractor will be subject to a 5% deduction from the payment for the affected phase.

Any violation of safety regulations on-site, or failure to comply with the client's safety standards, will incur a penalty of **5,000 SAR per incident**. Repeated violations will lead to a review of the contract.
